result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.max_flow()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute maximum flow from source to sink. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L26000-L26117){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.max_flow( source, sink, capacity=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Maximum flow](/assets/graphs/max-flow.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed network from source S to sink T through A and B. Each edge is labeled flow over capacity, and every edge carries flow, drawn in the accent color with width growing with the flow. The card lists the flow per edge, which totals 5." width="100%"} Finds the maximum amount of flow that can be sent from the source node to the sink node through the network. Uses the Edmonds-Karp algorithm (Ford-Fulkerson with BFS), which guarantees `O(VE²)` time complexity. For weighted graphs, edge weights are used as capacities by default. For unweighted graphs, each edge has capacity `1`. You can also specify a custom capacity attribute. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source node (integer ID or string label). [sink]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sink node (integer ID or string label). [capacity]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional name of edge attribute to use as capacity. If `None` (default), uses edge weights for weighted graphs, or `1.0` for unweighted graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping `edge_id -> flow amount` for edges with positive flow. Use `max_flow_value()` if you only need the total flow value. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If source or sink doesn't exist, they're the same node, or any capacity is negative. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The Edmonds-Karp variant of Ford-Fulkerson is used: at each step it augments along the *shortest* augmenting path (measured in edge count) found by BFS, which bounds the total number of augmentations by $O(V \cdot E)$ and gives an $O(V \cdot E^2)$ overall runtime regardless of the actual capacities. Undirected edges are internally treated as antiparallel pairs with equal capacity, and self-loops carry no flow. The max-flow min-cut theorem guarantees that the returned flow value equals the size of the minimum $s$-$t$ cut, which is what `get_min_cut_between()` reports; use `max_flow_value()` when only the number is needed. ## Examples {.doc-examples} With weighted edges acting as capacities, the flow algorithm finds how much can be routed from source to sink, splitting across parallel paths as needed: ::: {#3908339f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_node(label="S") # source .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="T") # sink .add_edge("S", "A", weight=10.0) .add_edge("S", "B", weight=5.0) .add_edge("A", "B", weight=15.0) .add_edge("A", "T", weight=10.0) .add_edge("B", "T", weight=10.0) ) flow_dict = graph.max_flow("S", "T") # Returns the number of edges carrying flow len(flow_dict) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: You can use any numeric edge attribute as capacity instead of weight, which is useful when weight already represents something else (like distance): ::: {#4c328d14 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B", bandwidth=100) .add_edge("B", "C", bandwidth=50) .add_edge("A", "C", bandwidth=30) ) flow_dict = graph.max_flow("A", "C", capacity="bandwidth") # Returns the number of edges carrying flow len(flow_dict) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: For unweighted graphs, every edge has capacity `1.0`, so max flow equals the number of edge-disjoint paths: ::: {#21ec2602 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_edge("S", "A", auto_create_nodes=True) .add_edge("S", "B", auto_create_nodes=True) .add_edge("A", "T", auto_create_nodes=True) .add_edge("B", "T", auto_create_nodes=True) ) # All 4 edges carry flow of 1.0 graph.max_flow("S", "T") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {3: 1.0, 1: 1.0, 4: 1.0, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: :::
